prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a hit while turning left in Houston, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1239; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you were involved in while turning left in Houston, Texas. Before we begin, do you consent to this statement being recorded?

A: Yes, I consent.

Q: Please state your full name and the best phone number to reach you.

A: [Claimant name] and the number is [phone number].

Q: Thank you. Can you describe what you were doing right before the collision?

A: I was driving north on a two-lane road and wanted to turn left into a shopping center parking lot. I slowed down, put on my turn signal, and waited for oncoming traffic to clear.

Q: What happened next?

A: There was a gap, so I started the turn. Then a car coming from the other direction hit the front driver's side of my vehicle. I didn't see it coming until right before impact.

Q: Did you see the other vehicle's headlights or signal before you turned?

A: I think it had its headlights on, but it was farther away than I expected. I misjudged the distance.

Q: Were you injured in the collision?

A: Yes. My lower back hurt right away, and it's gotten worse over the past few days. I have a stiff, sharp pain when I bend or lift.

Q: Have you seen a doctor or received any treatment?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic that same day. They said it looked like a back strain and gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and use ice.

Q: Do you have any prior back problems or injuries to that area?

A: No, nothing serious. I had some minor soreness years ago, but I never needed treatment for it.

Q: Is there anything else you would like to add to your statement?

A: No, I think that covers it. I just want to get my car repaired and get my back feeling better.

Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
